scope_plain: Every Mobile County voter. For 2026 all of Mobile County, including the whole City of Mobile, is in the 1st Congressional District; no part of the county votes in District 2.
office_explainer: Mobile's seat in the U.S. House. Votes on federal laws, taxes and spending; two-year term.
why_it_matters: Open seat: neither nominee holds it now. The map changed mid-year after the U.S. Supreme Court let Alabama use the Legislature's 2023 map, which put all of Mobile County back in District 1 and forced an Aug. 11 special primary. Under the 2024 map the City of Mobile was split between Districts 1 and 2 (about half each by area, per Census boundaries); now it is all in District 1.
incumbent: Barry Moore (running for U.S. Senate; not in this race)

candidates.name: Clyde Jones
candidates.background: Democratic nominee; qualified for the race as Clyde W. Jones, Jr. (WKRG). We found no campaign site or biography in our sources.

own_words.text: "Our constituents deserve to know our positions on the issues. I am challenging Mr. Carl to at least one debate, if not more."

candidates.name: Jerry Carl
candidates.background: Former member of the U.S. House and former president of the Mobile County Commission (2016). Won the Aug. 11, 2026 special Republican primary.

own_words.text: Says a vote for him is a vote for "years of trusted experience" in Congress (Lagniappe's paraphrase of Carl).

scope_plain: Every Mobile County voter, including the City of Mobile.
office_explainer: Runs county law enforcement, the Mobile County Metro Jail, and delivery of court papers.
why_it_matters: The main contested county race. The office has about 730 employees and a budget of about $75 million a year (FOX10). Sheriff Paul Burch seeks a second four-year term.

candidates.name: Pamela J. Laffitte
candidates.background: Retired Mobile County Sheriff's Office corrections sergeant (26 years, 6 months) and U.S. Air Force Reserve veteran; substitute teacher for Mobile County schools. Earlier a Prichard public safety dispatcher. A Democratic statewide nominee in 2022.

own_words.text: "Equipping all deputies and corrections officers with body-worn cameras (BWCs) to bring transparency."
Find budget room for more deputy positions, and make corrections officers sworn, certified "Deputy Corrections Officers."
"Establishing Public Oversight Committees comprised of constituents from each municipality within Mobile County." Also wants 24-hour bond hearings.

candidates.name: Paul Burch
candidates.background: Sheriff seeking a second term. Started as a police officer in Montgomery, then spent three decades rising through the Mobile County Sheriff's Office. Beat former Mobile Police Chief Paul Prine in the May Republican primary.

own_words.text: "Crime is really down, double digits." Credits partnerships with local and federal agencies.
"Protecting our children is our #1 priority," citing school resource deputies and Internet Crimes Against Children work.
Points to a new rural crime unit and deputies answering major crimes in Prichard: "I want to build on that."
